newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call marginally up, gilt yields steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call marginally up, gilt yields steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday in the 9.65-9.85 percent range, marginally up from the day's opening quotes of 9.50-9.75 percent, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade was done around 9.75 percent with stray deals at 10 percent, they said.
Dealers said the market seemed to have discounted the possibility of a one percentage point cut in banks' cash reserve requirements.
The Reserve Bank of India unveils its monetary policy for second half 1996/97 (April-March) on October 19 and many bankers expect it will announce a cut in cash reserve requirements.

Dealers said secondary market prices of government securities remained steady in moderate trade. They said banks were waiting to see the implication of the monetary policy on interest rates before taking fresh positions.
"After a bout of speculation in the last two weeks, the market has become more cautious," said a dealer.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock traded at 13.17 percent against its last traded 13.16 percent while the 13.70 percent 1999 stock remained unchanged at 13.48 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 18-20 percent range.
